points: The Q3 2026 print will show whether Marsh can sustain the 5% underlying revenue growth reported in Q2 and turn it into faster operating-income growth than the 4% seen last quarter, which is the core lever for the long case.

MRSH reports before its insurance-broker peers — GSHD, ERIE, RYAN and AJG all print later — so its guidance and tone will set the sector read-through and can either reinforce or weaken the long setup before those names report.

Consensus already prices FY1/FY2 EPS growth of about 7.2% and 9.2%, and the 30-day revision tape is strongly positive at 17 up versus 2 down; Q3 needs to validate that analysts are not overestimating the earnings path.

Valuation is fair versus the theme — P/E is 0.9x the median but PEG is 1.2x the median — so the long case depends on the roughly 9.2% FY2 growth outlook looking credible rather than on multiple expansion.

With the insurance-broker theme cold and breadth flat, MRSH’s own estimate momentum is the main driver; the Q3 call must show stable organic growth and no deterioration in the outlook that would break that momentum.

The following quarters set up around the FY2 growth acceleration to roughly 9.2%; if Q3 guidance implies that pickup is intact, the path to further FY2 estimate revisions remains supportive for the long.
watch: Q3 underlying revenue growth holds at or above the 5% reported in Q2 — supports the long.
Operating income growth accelerates from the 4% reported in Q2 — supports the long.
FY2 EPS growth outlook stays near 9.2% and consensus estimates are not cut — supports the long.
The 1.2x PEG premium to the theme is justified by sustained organic growth and stable guidance — supports the long.
